# Step 1: soft-switching operating mode (generated by r1_softsw.py)

1. Design sweep (analytic, tcm.py, calibrated to r1_turnoff.py): inductance, snubber capacitance
   across each IGBT and the dead time allowed for the valley transition (which sets the reverse
   current I_zvs); losses of the bridge at the M15 operating points.
2. The chosen design at every M15 operating point, for V_ANODE (330 uH) and V_SCREEN (680 uH):
   frequency, currents, losses per device and in the inductor, junction temperatures, against M15.
   Variants: frequency from the voltage only (no load adaptation), fixed dead time, hard-switched
   reference.
3. Switching-level check with the calibrated IGBT model (ngspice, swmodel.py): one bridge in TCM at
   the chosen frequency and edge timing, the snubber capacitors, the UCC21520 drive as drawn
   (15 ohm, 10 kohm, 1 nF G-E, bootstrap), raw side as drawn; the output is C1 (100 uF) with the load
   current (the rest of the filter does not change the bridge's currents). Read: zero-voltage turn-on
   (switch-node voltage left across the device when its gate crosses V_th), losses per device,
   bootstrap, the switch node dv/dt and the Miller bump on the off device.
4. The MOSFET option (class-typical 650 V superjunction and SiC values, analytic).

## The IGBT's turn-off with snubber capacitors (r1_turnoff.py, swmodel IGBT calibrated to the datasheet, 125 C, 420 V, 15 ohm + 1 nF G-E)

Turn-off energy (uJ) / time from the gate command to the node at the other rail (ns). Cs is across each IGBT (the node sees 2 Cs + the devices' own charge + 20 pF). Cs = 0 is the hard turn-off (the datasheet's Eoff: 20 uJ at 2 A, 150 C, 48 ohm).

| I (A) | Cs 0 pF | Cs 100 pF | Cs 220 pF | Cs 470 pF | Cs 1000 pF |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | 1.6 / 205 | 1.1 / 995 | 0.9 / 1951 | 0.3 / > 2000 | 0.1 / > 2000 |
| 0.2 | 2.6 / 129 | 1.5 / 534 | 1.2 / 1005 | 0.9 / 1997 | 0.4 / > 2000 |
| 0.3 | 3.6 / 101 | 1.9 / 379 | 1.4 / 693 | 1.1 / 1349 | 0.7 / > 2000 |
| 0.5 | 5.9 / 78 | 3.2 / 253 | 2.1 / 443 | 1.5 / 836 | 1.2 / 1684 |
| 0.75 | 8.9 / 66 | 5.2 / 189 | 3.4 / 320 | 2.2 / 579 | 1.6 / 1146 |
| 1.0 | 12.0 / 59 | 7.6 / 156 | 5.2 / 257 | 3.1 / 452 | 2.1 / 876 |
| 1.5 | 17.6 / 53 | 11.9 / 119 | 8.7 / 190 | 5.2 / 322 | 3.3 / 607 |
| 2.0 | 21.4 / 50 | 15.4 / 101 | 11.9 / 154 | 7.6 / 256 | 4.6 / 470 |
| 2.5 | 25.1 / 49 | 18.7 / 89 | 15.0 / 132 | 9.8 / 214 | 6.0 / 387 |
| 3.0 | 28.3 / 48 | 21.4 / 82 | 18.0 / 117 | 12.6 / 188 | 7.8 / 332 |

Reading: the snubber only slows the voltage rise under the tail current; the tail charge itself (about 30 nC/A in the calibrated model, consistent with the datasheet's 20 uJ at 2 A) stays. 220 pF cuts the turn-off energy by 45 % at 2 A, 470 pF by 65 %, 1 nF by 80 %, but the valley edge then needs 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.9 A of reverse current to swing the node in 500 ns, and that reverse current is ripple the IGBT turns off again at the peak.

Reading: the turn-off energy is roughly proportional to the current turned off, and in TCM the current turned off per second is the ripple slope V_o (1 - D) / L, whatever the frequency. So the IGBT bridge's loss at mid voltage is set by L alone (about 7 uJ per ampere x V_o (1 - D) / L), while the frequency at the top of the range falls as 1 / L: the two ends pull L in opposite directions. Raising f_max does not lower the mid-voltage loss (it only lowers the ripple and the core loss).

## 2. Chosen design

V_ANODE: L = 220 uH (ETD39 N97, 36 turns litz 0.8 mm2), Cs = 220 pF C0G 1 kV across each IGBT, valley dead time up to 600 ns (I_zvs = 0.38 A), f = clamp(f_TCM, 40 kHz, 150 kHz), load-adaptive. V_SCREEN: L = 470 uH (ETD39 N97, 52 turns litz 0.5 mm2), same rest. Tj at 80 C local air: on an SK 104 38.1 mm (12 K/W + 1 K/W pad + 2.2 K/W) or free-standing (62 K/W).

## 4. The MOSFET option (analytic, class-typical values to confirm on a datasheet)

Same TCM law, L = 150 uH, f 25-300 kHz (200 kHz keeps 4 gates inside the +12 V budget), 300 ns transitions. Under ZVS a MOSFET's turn-off is nearly lossless (the channel stops in about 10 ns and the current moves into C_oss), so the loss is conduction only.
